item.title: [New] Microsoft Threat Intelligence: the ARTEX agentic penetration-testing framework is abused by Storm-0940, Storm-3358, Onyx Sleet, Pearl Sleet, Crystal Typhoon and Salt Typhoon
item.description:
Six named actors, two of them state-sponsored, use one agentic framework to speed up reconnaissance and credential attacks; this brief already tracks Storm-0940's ARTEX use against ConnectWise apps (storm-0940-artex-connectwise-2026-10-21).

Threat Intel · Read the post for its detections and hunting guidance and compare it with the Storm-0940 item already in this brief.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Defender for Endpoint on Windows Enterprise multi-session: every user of the Azure Virtual Desktop VMs must be licensed; the Defender for Servers option is gone from the page
item.description:
A multi-session AVD pool covered only by Defender for Servers no longer matches Microsoft's documented licensing for Defender for Endpoint.

MDE · Check how AVD multi-session hosts are licensed for Defender for Endpoint and confirm the per-user licence position with your Microsoft contact.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [Due in 5 days] Defender for Identity retires two classic alerts at the end of November: Remote code execution attempt and Suspected identity theft (pass-the-hash)
item.description:
Two identity-attack detections disappear from the SOC queue; any analytics rule, playbook or SLA keyed on their alert titles goes silent, and pass-the-hash on hosts without MDE is no longer alerted at all.

MDI · deadline 2026-11-30 · Before 30 November create the Advanced Hunting custom detection from Microsoft's RemoteCodeExecution query, confirm MDE covers every DC and tier-0 host for pass-the-hash, and repoint Sentinel rules and playbooks that match the two classic alert names.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [Due in 7 days] Defender RBAC is switched on automatically for Defender and Sentinel portal experiences, about 30 days after an in-portal notice, from early December 2026
item.description:
After activation, Defender and Sentinel portal access is decided by imported Defender RBAC roles, not by the legacy workload roles a SOC audited; an import that maps an analyst too broadly or too narrowly changes incident and email access without any new grant being made.

Defender XDR · deadline 2026-12-02 · When the banner appears, review every imported role and scope under Permissions > Roles in the Defender portal, test an analyst and a Security Reader account against email, device and Sentinel views, move any role automation to the Defender RBAC Graph API, and update runbooks before 2 December 2026.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [Due in 6 days] Security Operator loses default access to email threat policies and the Tenant Allow/Block List under Defender Unified RBAC, now from early December
item.description:
Adding a block entry to the Tenant Allow/Block List is a routine containment step in a phishing incident. An analyst who holds only Security Operator will find that step denied mid-incident some day in November, with no error that names this change.

Defender XDR · deadline 2026-12-01 · List who holds Entra Security Operator and uses it for email threat policies or the Tenant Allow/Block List; before November assign those people the Unified RBAC permissions Core security settings and Detection tuning, or a role that includes them, and test a block entry with a Security Operator-only account.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [Due in 6 days] App Governance permissions change for three Entra roles as Defender XDR Unified RBAC takes over
item.description:
Two compliance roles silently lose an app-governance capability and one security role gains it: an app-governance policy nobody can edit, or one an unexpected role can now edit, is a control gap either way.

Defender XDR · deadline 2026-12-01 · Before early December, list who reaches App Governance through Compliance Administrator, Compliance Data Administrator or Cloud App Security Administrator, review custom Defender XDR Unified RBAC roles for Defender for Cloud Apps, and reassign affected people to a supported Entra role or a custom Unified RBAC role on least privilege.

item.title: [New] SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents: a new advanced hunting table records deepfake (synthetic media) detections in Microsoft Teams calls and meetings
item.description:
Voice and video impersonation of executives and help-desk staff is the social-engineering path behind several recent intrusions; this is the first table that records it as data a SOC can hunt and alert on.

Defender XDR · If a detection engine is approved, add a custom detection on IsMalicious == true joined to CallActivityEvents, and route it to the team that handles payment-fraud and help-desk verification.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Custom detection rules map up to four identifiers per entity and the same entity type more than once (preview from 17 November 2026)
item.description:
Richer entity mapping is what correlation, automatic attack disruption and the new alert grouping key on; a rule that maps only one weak identifier groups and correlates badly.

Defender XDR · Review the custom detections that drive automated actions and add the stronger identifiers (object ID, SID, device ID) to their entities before turning on alert grouping.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Custom detection rules can group their own alerts into one incident by time frame and matching entities (preview from 17 November 2026)
item.description:
Grouping changes how many incidents a noisy rule opens and how the queue reads; a rule set to 'group all alerts into one incident' can fold an unrelated second intrusion into an incident an analyst already triaged, and a closed incident is never reopened, so a matching alert lands in a new one.

Defender XDR · Leave grouping off on high-severity rules until tested; for noisy rules, choose 'all entities match' rather than 'group all', and document the time frame so the SOC knows why an incident holds many alerts.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Defender portal navigation reorganised in preview: Microsoft Sentinel pages move out of their own section into the areas where they are used
item.description:

item.description:
